reader.requirement: After a successful REWRITE of a relative file the record need not remain in the record area, except that when the file is named in a SAME RECORD AREA clause the released record stays available in the area and as a record of every other file in that clause.
reader.edition-search: grep Edition|DialectLevel|DialectBehavior|IsActive over SequentialIoEmitter.cs (only NamedRecordEntry and the registrations, not on this path), KeyedIoEmitter.cs (only EmitRegistration) and FileModel.cs#OutOfLineRecordsOfArea/SameRecordAreaPeers: the SAME RECORD AREA sharing is one backing at every edition, and the out-of-line store is emitted on the same compile-time test.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf07_08 covers two relative files with character records; not a peer with an ODO record, a three-file clause, a signed COMP-3 field, or the unsuccessful REWRITE

probes.expected: SAME RECORD AREA FOR RA (relative dynamic) SB (sequential, ODO record) RC (relative sequential): after the successful REWRITE the record is in RA-REC and visible through RC-REC and SB-REC's count field; the failed REWRITE (23) leaves the area as moved and the file record 2 unchanged

citations.check: OK  §1985:VIII.4.6.4 GR4  (4.6.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR4

reader.notes: Character-window records of a SAME RECORD AREA share one backing, so the released record is available to every peer without a store; an out-of-line peer gets the emitted EmitReleasedRecordAlsoAvailable store on a successful status only. The 'no longer available' half imposes nothing observable, so any area content conforms there.
